findings.title: Google Calendar credential key is saved as Zod SafeParseReturnType instead of credential data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token object itself. Here, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is passed directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, which corrupts the stored credential and causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a Zod validation error on every subsequent Google Calendar call.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] which defines literal "[object Object]" key
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances at module load time, producing the literal property key `"[object Object]"`. As a result, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` requires a numeric property literally named `"[object Object]"` and strips all other properties (including `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, and `refresh_token`), so `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will always fail when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is active.

findings.title: Missing import of prisma in SalesforceCalendarService causes ReferenceError
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is not imported anywhere in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`. Instantiating `SalesforceCalendarService` will fail at runtime with `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`. Additionally, lines 75-84 call `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping it in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and line 106 passes the stale `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection`.

findings.title: credentialId passed instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens in Zoho Bigin
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`, and sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to the sync endpoint. In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (the primary key of the `Credential` row) is passed as the third argument instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the wrong user ID.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response incompatible with callers expecting SDK/axios return shapes
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. However, several callers expect the return value of their SDK/HTTP client inside `refreshFunction`: `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (gaxios response), `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` directly on the returned object, `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `.data` (axios response). None of these properties exist on a `fetch` `Response`, so token refresh with credential syncing enabled will throw or store `undefined` tokens for all four integrations.

findings.title: appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name, not app.slug, breaking lookup for several apps
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` keys are generated from the app directory names in `packages/app-store` (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `zoomvideo`, `larkcalendar`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` stores the `config.json` slug (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `zoom`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` on line 50 returns `undefined` for all of these apps, causing the webhook to return 404 "App not found" whenever credentials are synced for Google Calendar, Office 365 Calendar, MS Teams, Zoom, Lark Calendar, etc.
